newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba judge to rule on UGG poison pill Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba judge to rule on UGG poison pill Tuesday.

text.p: Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench Judge John Scollin said Thursday he will rule Tuesday on applications that United Grain Growers Ltd poison pill was triggered by a hostile takeover bid and the bidders' claim the pill is invalid.
"You will have your answer Tuesday morning," Scollin told court.

Privately held Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators made a C$172 million hostile takeover bid for UGG February 20th when they raised their stake in Canada's third largest grain handling firm to 14.98 percent of UGG's 12.5 million limited outstanding common voting shares and announced they'd entered into an irrevockable lock-up agreement with U.S. mutual fund Lindner for another 6.4 percent of shares.
UGG's board of directors adopted a shareholder rights plan Feb 14 granting any shareholder other than a hostile bidder the option to purchase 8.5 more shares for each one already held at C$5.88 each.
UGG shares traded at C$13.75 in light volume on the Toronto Stock Exchange most of Thursday. The Pools' bid is at C$13.75 a share.
Lindner lawyer Randy McNicol told court the mutual fund "would never have entered the agreement if it knew UGG was going to say it (lock-up agreement) triggers the poison pill."
McNicol estimated Lindner's holdings in UGG would decrease in value by C$5.8 million from a massive dilution of UGG shares.
He added that a clause in the lock-up agreement with the Pools gave Lindner the option to withdraw from the deal.
UGG lawyer John Scurfield said the TSE's request to have UGG shareholders vote on the rights plan by August 14 was proof the poison pill is valid.
Pools lawyer Blair Graham told court the lock-up agreement did not acquire Lindner's beneficial voting rights and that the poison pill was not valid.
Scollin told all parties he would forward his ruling to them Tuesday morning. Queen's Bench information office opens at 0900 CST.
Lindner is a unit of U.S.-based Ryback Management Group.
